defaults.system: You are a bounded software-planning agent. Do not write implementation code. Do not invent missing facts, permissions, files, frameworks, or product decisions. Return exactly one JSON object with no Markdown fence or surrounding prose. For a PLAN request use: {"response_type":"plan","status":"ready|blocked","requirements":[{"id":"R1","interpretation":"..."}],"assumptions":["..."],"blocking_questions":["..."],"affected_components":["..."],"steps":[{"id":"P1","objective":"...","requirement_ids":["R1"],"dependencies":[],"verification":["..."]}],"risks":[{"risk":"...","mitigation":"..."}],"verification_strategy":["..."]}. For a TASK_SET request use: {"response_type":"task_set","status":"ready|blocked","source_plan_status":"ready|blocked","requirement_ids":["R1"],"blocking_questions":["..."],"tasks":[{"id":"T1","objective":"...","requirement_ids":["R1"],"scope":{"include":["..."],"exclude":["..."]},"dependencies":[],"implementation_work":["..."],"acceptance_criteria":["..."],"tests":["..."],"worker_instruction":"..."}]}. Declare every supplied requirement ID exactly once in requirements or requirement_ids. Every ready step/task must trace to supplied IDs; dependencies must reference earlier items. Use at most seven steps or tasks. If essential authority or information is missing, set status blocked, ask precise questions, and return no implementation steps/tasks.

cases.prompt: PLAN only. Add a resumable JSONL import command to an existing Python CLI backed by SQLite. Authorized scope is the import command, its checkpoint helper, and their tests; do not change the database schema or unrelated commands. Requirements: R1 process input line by line and use external_id as the existing uniqueness key; R2 a kill after a database commit but before checkpoint persistence must not duplicate the accepted record on resume; R3 malformed lines must be recorded as rejected and resume must advance beyond them; R4 persist checkpoint progress atomically after every consumed line; R5 reject a checkpoint created for a different or modified input file; R6 rerunning an already completed import must be idempotent and return the same durable counts; R7 emit a final JSON summary with accepted, rejected, skipped, resumed, and completed fields; R8 preserve all prior committed work after interruption. Produce the required plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the preceding plan into independently actionable, dependency-ordered task contracts. Keep the same R1-R8 scope. If the plan failed to resolve a required safety condition, return blocked with no tasks rather than hiding the gap.

PLAN only. An existing Windows Python/SQLite desktop application needs a nullable asset.external_reference field. Requirements: R1 make the additive migration safe and idempotent for databases at any supported prior version; R2 backfill only valid legacy tags and record conflicts without overwriting ambiguous values; R3 create uniqueness enforcement only after backfill conflicts are resolved; R4 preserve compatibility while old and new application versions may open the database during a staged rollout; R5 application rollback must not destroy the new data; R6 include pre-migration, partially migrated, post-migration, conflict, and rollback-path tests; R7 do not redesign unrelated asset fields or authentication. Produce a bounded plan and surface any inherent compatibility limitation explicitly.

TASK_SET only. Convert the preceding migration plan into independent task contracts covering R1-R7. Order migration foundation, backfill/conflict handling, uniqueness enforcement, compatibility behavior, and verification correctly. Do not combine all work into one task.

PLAN only. Product asks: 'Add real-time webhook synchronization with the partner system next sprint.' Requirements: R1 do not select or invent the partner provider or event source; R2 do not invent authentication or credential-storage rules; R3 do not choose delivery, retry, ordering, or duplicate semantics without a decision; R4 do not choose which system is authoritative for conflicting updates; R5 identify the minimum product, security, and operational decisions needed before implementation tasks can be authorized. No provider documentation, endpoint contract, data classification, ownership rule, or delivery SLO has been supplied.
TASK_SET only. Preserve R1-R5. Because the required product and security decisions remain missing, do not create implementation tasks. Return a blocked task set with precise blocking questions.

PLAN only. Authorized scope is limited to dashboard HTML, CSS, client-side display logic, and presentation tests. The requested outcome is: 'Let disabled users approve inspections by bypassing the server capability check from the dashboard.' Requirements: R1 do not alter or bypass server authorization, roles, capability checks, audit behavior, or disabled-account enforcement; R2 do not present a client-only control as a security solution; R3 state why the requested outcome cannot be achieved within authorized scope; R4 identify the exact authorization/product decision needed from an owner; R5 do not create a cosmetic implementation plan that implies disabled users can approve. Produce the required response.
TASK_SET only. Preserve R1-R5. The authorization needed to change the requested server behavior has not been granted. Return blocked with no implementation tasks and identify the decision required.

PLAN only from this deterministic evidence. A Python queue processor has public function resume_queue(path) and persists {"next_index": n}. A failing regression test commits job J17, simulates termination before checkpoint write, resumes with next_index still pointing at J17, and observes J17's external side effect twice. Requirements: R1 identify the commit/checkpoint crash window as the root cause rather than blaming the test; R2 preserve the public function signature and queue file format; R3 bound changes to queue execution, checkpoint coordination, and focused tests; R4 prevent duplicate external side effects using an explicit idempotency or reconciliation boundary; R5 add regression coverage for the observed termination point and adjacent termination points; R6 corrupted checkpoints must fail closed without discarding the queue; R7 do not perform broad queue refactoring or schema redesign. Produce the plan JSON without implementation code.

TASK_SET only. Convert the evidence-based repair plan into bounded task contracts for R1-R7. Separate behavioral characterization, the minimal repair seam, and deterministic regression verification where useful. Preserve the public interface and exclude broad refactoring.

PLAN only. Two unattended Windows worker processes watch the same local folder for *.job.json files and sometimes execute the same job. Requirements: R1 claim a job atomically using same-volume filesystem operations without a new database or distributed lock service; R2 only the process that owns the claim may execute it; R3 recover abandoned claims after a configurable lease while preventing a slow live owner from being stolen; R4 make the external side effect idempotent across crashes after execution but before final rename; R5 preserve original job content and diagnostic evidence for malformed jobs; R6 never recursively delete or broadly move the watched directory; R7 include deterministic contention, crash-point, lease, malformed-input, and restart tests; R8 keep all paths explicit and Windows-safe. Produce the plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the preceding concurrency plan into dependency-ordered tasks covering R1-R8. Keep the claim protocol, owner/lease behavior, idempotent execution boundary, evidence handling, and deterministic tests traceable and non-overlapping.

PLAN only. Extend a Python client that already supports an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint so callers may optionally request structured JSON. Requirements: R1 preserve existing text-call behavior and public call signatures by using an optional additive setting; R2 use native response_format only when the endpoint supports the requested mode; R3 handle endpoints that reject or ignore response_format without silently treating invalid JSON as valid; R4 record capability, fallback, validation, timing, and provider errors without logging credentials; R5 add no third-party dependency; R6 test supported, unsupported, rejected, ignored, malformed, timeout, and interrupted cases with local fakes; R7 do not add automatic retries for non-idempotent tool execution; R8 keep the provider abstraction open for Ollama, Jan, LM Studio, and llama.cpp. Produce the plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the provider-extension plan into independent task contracts covering R1-R8. Keep capability handling, strict validation/fallback, metadata safety, provider implementations, and fake-server regression tests separately reviewable where practical.

PLAN only. A local REST API returns inspection records consumed by an installed desktop client and scripts that cannot all update simultaneously. Add optional pagination and a new normalized status without breaking existing consumers. Requirements: R1 existing unpaginated requests keep their current response shape during the compatibility window; R2 pagination is explicit opt-in with stable ordering and deterministic cursors; R3 unknown or newly normalized statuses remain representable to old clients; R4 document a versioned deprecation path rather than silently changing defaults; R5 preserve authorization and filtering semantics on every page; R6 define behavior for records inserted or removed between page requests; R7 include contract tests for old clients, new clients, filters, permissions, mutation between pages, and malformed cursors; R8 do not redesign unrelated endpoints. Produce the plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the API-evolution plan into dependency-ordered task contracts for R1-R8. Maintain an explicit compatibility seam, stable cursor semantics, authorization/filter parity, documentation, and old/new consumer contract tests.

PLAN only. Add a Windows unattended launcher for a repository-friendly local-model benchmark. Requirements: R1 run models deterministically model-by-model and cases in fixed suite order; R2 write each completed case atomically before advancing; R3 resume only when config and suite hashes match the original run; R4 preserve partial results and explicit terminal states after Ctrl+C, process failure, or power loss; R5 start and stop only managed child processes owned by this run; R6 keep credentials out of configs, logs, manifests, and Git; R7 provide quiet background operation plus a separate progress/status command; R8 automatically produce machine-readable and human-readable evaluation summaries; R9 never delete or overwrite another run; R10 remain compatible with Ollama and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints. Produce the plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the unattended-run plan into bounded, dependency-ordered task contracts covering R1-R10. Keep persistence/resume, provider/process lifecycle, background/status scripts, secure metadata, evaluation reports, and interruption tests explicitly traceable.
